description.narrative:
Thought leadership in smallholder resilience Goal: Develop thought leadership on farmer income and climate resilience through enhanced measurement methodologies.
Strategic angle: i) Amplify the narrative and actual impact of existing programs; ii) Leverage Oxfaminternal learning agenda externally; iii) Increase recognition as thought leaders on Living Income and data analytics; iv) Make LINK a more attractive knowledge partner to NGOs, governments and the private sector.
Existing opportunities: i) Leverage ongoing workby the Fair Value Chain and Food Systems team on Living Income in cocoa and rice; ii) Combine LINK unit's methodologic robustness with new insights on systems thinking. Iii) Strengthen campaigning agenda to challenge private sectorsustainability programs How do proposed activities complement, add value to current program / goal unit priorities. Systemic change is a difficult topic to measure,but what we can measure is the impact we have in our programs on farmer income. Currently, we work in the Living Income (LI) paradigm that measures whether average farmers can have access to a decent life. In real life, even when average farmers are supposed to earn a LI, actual farming households do not feel a significant change in their livelihood. This is partly because what we measure does not fit the farming reality on the ground. The sector uses assessments that are short-term focused and do not consider a risk analysis. These assessments cannot be a good predictor of future longer-term farming income. We need to understand how farming family’s income is vulnerable to shocks and how our programs are benefiting long-lasting systems change.
This proposal aligns with our activist identity and decolonising mission because it challengesexisting power structures, promotes fair resource distribution and supports marginalised communities, reinforcing our commitment to systemic change. How do proposed activities seize a specific funding opportunity to strengthen the pipeline. For our work on partnerships with the private sector three main elements are vital for the private sector to work with us: 1) Expertise, 2) Sector recognition and 3) resource efficiency. With this proposal the program departmentinvests in the first 2.
For our communication to donors, it is important to be able to show the impact of our work even when they might not yield direct effects. Most of our interventions are targeting root causes of systemic failure but cannot show how (much) they have impact on actual farmer livelihood. This improved ability will make our programs and our ToCs more attractive to donors.
For the LINK department the value proposition improves even further. It currently is a very resource efficient impact and learning partner but might not be well known in the sector for its research capabilities and thought leadership. This project would improve ourpipeline towards NGOs, governments, and the private sector as a knowledge partner. How do proposed activities foster collaboration?(Specify if among program units/departments/regional or country offices, confederation leads or other partners) Complex challenges require multidisciplinary approaches and diverse perspectives to be effectively addressed. Hence, collaborating on the edge of thought leadership between units would be a unique opportunity. FVCFS has the knowledge of Living Income and farming livelihood, while the LINK unit understands research methods. Our shared goal of working on systemic change and understanding how we can measure this brings us together in this first attempt to work closely on a new knowledge product. This could also be leveraged by working with colleagues from GREEN to add a climate resilience lens to have a comprehensive systems approach.
Moreover, it could be a great exploratory process to dive into the methods implemented internally and externally, creating a space for discussion and co-creation. We planto bring representatives of different projects to create a shared understanding and think along the best way to enhance measurementand implementation. Through these actions, we will contribute to the learning agenda of different actors, leading the journey of continuous reflection, learning and adaptation.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
